layers.gate: Match transactions, committed records, full search relevance, filters, update visibility and crash recovery under a fixed memory/storage allowance.
layers.label: Local storage & search

layers.decision: Use verified HTTP transfers as the control. Compare range/delta or peer transfer only with the same trusted identity, complete content and recovery policy.
layers.gate: Reject changed validators and corrupt chunks; handle ignored ranges, disconnects, retries, cancellation and source mutation without mixing versions.
layers.label: Downloads, transfer & sync

layers.decision: Keep API semantics and deployment budgets fixed. Language/runtime and framework changes are distinct variables; shared service storage is a separate cohort from embedded storage.
layers.gate: Preserve validation, auth boundaries, errors, consistency, timeouts and load behavior; report tail latency, useful throughput and full operational cost.
layers.label: APIs & shared services

layers.decision: Combine versioned update metadata, artifact identity, provenance and platform installation deliberately. A signature alone does not provide rollback/freeze protection or atomic installation.
layers.gate: Reject expired, replayed, wrong-signer and mismatched artifacts; test rotation, delegation, interrupted updates, downgrade policy and restoration of user data.
layers.label: Signed distribution & updates

layers.decision: Compare a pinned current build with incremental, hermetic or reproducibility tooling. Keep clean, warmed and changed-input builds in separate lanes.
layers.gate: Preserve emitted artifacts, diagnostics and dependency integrity; verify environment locks, cache invalidation, binary differences and CI portability.
layers.label: Builds & reproducibility

layers.decision: Use end-to-end tests and saved traces as controls. Add replay, fuzzing and model exploration for explicit fault classes; each tool has its own coverage limits.
layers.gate: Retain seeded faults, false positives, missed defects, trace loss, instrumentation overhead and replay limits; a clean run is not a proof of correctness.
layers.label: Testing, profiling & correctness

layers.decision: Treat AI as an optional feature or engineering tool with a declared task and budget. Compare full model/runtime/agent configurations rather than framework names alone.
layers.gate: Require useful held-out task quality, privacy/tool boundaries, completed outputs, cost and latency budgets; keep publisher scores separate from local reproduction.
layers.label: Optional AI & developer tools

layers.decision: Choose a local journal or service workflow to fit the deployment boundary. Do not introduce a remote orchestrator merely to run a desktop job.
layers.gate: Recover from crashes at every state transition with explicit idempotency, retry, cancellation and external side-effect rules; retain acknowledged work and full diagnostics.
layers.label: Background work & recovery

layers.decision: Use the same complete benchmark/telemetry dataset and query semantics. Compare engines and storage formats as separate variables.
layers.gate: Preserve values, nulls, ordering and full aggregates; require completion beyond RAM with fixed resource limits and retained spill/error evidence.
layers.label: Analytics & result formats

controls: The actual target's current embedded store, revision and record/index contract.
The same committed transaction boundaries and failure model; cache-only completion is not a control.
Current authoritative catalog. KV and SQL designs are separate cohorts with equivalent application indexes and transaction boundaries.
test_plans.decision: which embedded store fits a desktop catalog's durable metadata workload?
gates: identical committed records and warnings after reopen; declared transaction boundaries; no acknowledged-write loss under the selected failure model.
Fix acknowledged-write durability and ensure error propagation.
Keep index construction and maintenance inside timing.
Retain long-reader growth, compaction and corruption cases.
Never treat technical tags or prereleases as the stable baseline.
Reject relaxed-acknowledgement gains and candidates missing required SQL/extension/transaction behavior.
metrics: import-to-durable-completion time, p95/p99 lookup latency, memory, storage amplification, recovery time, and integration burden. A faster cache-only write path is ineligible.
protocol: Compare the current store with SQLite, redb, and RocksDB implementations of the same record and index contract. Use small, typical, and large catalogs; imports, indexed lookups, concurrent readers, deletion, rename, and interrupted transactions. Put shared PostgreSQL service operation in a separate deployment cohort.

Prerequisites: a publishable representative corpus, pinned source revisions and toolchains, supported target hardware, and an existing complete-output oracle. Declare numeric CPU, queue, memory, disk and responsiveness budgets before execution.
Workload: Imports, updates, deletes, long readers, conflict bursts, compaction, disk-full and injected write errors, crash/reopen and rollback migration.

Separate cold and warm conditions and retain at least five independent repeated samples per configuration, including failed or cancelled runs. Record OS, CPU, storage, power mode, thread counts and cache policy.

Retain full raw outputs, warnings, validation failures, resource traces, configuration and corpus hashes. Apply correctness and resource gates before comparing performance; this plan records no execution or result.
test_plans.title: Local catalog transactions

controls: The current complete query implementation over one fixed dataset and memory allowance.
Hold the storage format fixed when comparing engines; compare Vortex and Parquet as a separate variable.
test_plans.decision: how should Atlas inspect large benchmark and telemetry datasets on a developer machine?
gates: full result equivalence, explicit null/number/order semantics, successful out-of-core completion, and identical projections.
metrics: cold and warmed query time, peak RSS, spill bytes, bytes read, and total analysis time. Retain unsupported-query results instead of shrinking the workload to each engine's strengths.
protocol: Compare DuckDB, Polars, and DataFusion with equivalent scans, joins, selective filters, and high-cardinality aggregations. Include a corpus larger than the fixed memory allowance. Treat Vortex versus Parquet as a separately declared storage-format variable rather than changing engine and format together.
test_plans.title: Local result analytics under memory pressure

controls: The target's current parser and full input-to-validated-output path.
Keep the retained warmed JSON measurements as historical evidence in their existing cohorts.
test_plans.decision: does a faster parser help the target without changing its data contract?
gates: declared duplicate-key policy, exact required integer behavior, Unicode handling, depth limits, nonfinite-number rules, complete outputs, and failure reporting.
metrics: input-to-validated-result time, cold cost, memory, and per-case semantic outcomes. A library can be ineligible for one numeric contract while remaining a candidate for another.
protocol: Extend the earlier stdlib/orjson/ujson study with representative publishable files, cold imports/startup, file I/O, downstream validation, allocations, and peak RSS. Retain the earlier lab's distinct nine operation/workload cohorts; do not mix their warmed samples into new trials.
test_plans.title: Python JSON compatibility and complete application cost

controls: The pinned current implementation of the complete scan/import journey.
A fresh complete inventory with the same hidden-file, ignore, path, metadata, diagnostic and output policy.
test_plans.decision: would a language/runtime change improve an actual file-processing journey enough to justify migration?
gates: complete output hashes, preserved unreadable-file and malformed-input diagnostics, bounded resource use, cancellation/restart correctness, and target-platform packaging.
metrics: cold full completion, steady-state completion, p95 UI impact, CPU, I/O, RSS, and build/deployment effort. Microkernel speed alone cannot decide the migration.
protocol: Compare the pinned current implementation with bounded Rust, Zig, or Go prototypes of one complete scan/import operation. Keep filesystem fixtures, filtering, metadata, archive handling, hashing, warning generation, cancellation, and result serialization fixed. Treat a compiler update separately from a rewrite.

Split the workload into controlled variables: WalkDir versus `ignore` traversal with all required hidden/ignore filtering explicitly disabled; fresh scan versus watcher/USN reconciliation; hash choice; chunking/delta; compression; and archive implementation. Keep the complete end-to-end run as the deciding outcome. Include symlinks/reparse points, hard links, case/Unicode collisions, unreadable entries, concurrent mutation, archive bombs and traversal attempts. Never infer multi-file durability from a single replacement primitive.
test_plans.title: Complete native file pipeline

controls: The same parser/transform plugin running natively with an explicitly fixed host API.
Separate in-process VM, native helper process and service deployment cohorts.
The current runtime with the same validated modules, host ABI, resource limits and granted capabilities.
Interpreter, AOT and JIT configurations are independent cohorts with compile/setup work counted.
test_plans.decision: can portable plugins retain required behavior within the target's security and latency budget?
gates: output parity, declared host capabilities, bounded memory, correct cancellation and traps, and required OS/toolchain support.
Identical plugin outputs, error/trap transport, validation and permitted host-call behavior.
Denied file/network/handle operations remain denied, memory/time bounds work and crashed plugins do not corrupt host state.
Unsupported WASI/Component features are explicit ineligibility, not silently removed functionality.
metrics: compilation cost separately from startup, boundary-copy cost, throughput, RSS, and portability failures. Host APIs are part of the security boundary and must remain fixed.
Cold load-to-ready, complete operation p95/p99, host-boundary overhead, compile time, code/runtime size, RSS and recovery latency.
protocol: Run the same parser/transform plugin natively and in Wasmtime using a fixed WASI component interface. Add Spin only for a service-shaped workload with equivalent networking semantics. Test large streams, cancellation, denied capabilities, malformed inputs, and memory exhaustion.

Add Luau only as a separate embedded-language configuration with a fixed host API. Compare AppContainer/LPAC on eligible Windows systems and bubblewrap on eligible Linux systems for owned native-helper workloads. Do not treat an in-process VM, a native plugin ABI, an OS sandbox and an updater as equivalent security boundaries. Pin supported WASI/runtime/toolchain combinations; current 0.3 availability does not imply every browser or language path supports it.
Pin canonical runtime release, compiler, enabled features and host imports. Use the same small and large plugin modules with compute and host-call-heavy work.
Test malformed modules, traps, infinite loops, allocation growth, invalid handles and cancellation during a host call.
Count AOT generation and trust/distribution requirements separately; retain runtime validation and current memory-safety fixes.
Record feature gaps and target platforms. Run repeated calls and teardown/reload cycles to detect leaks and stale handles.
test_plans.title: Portable sandboxed plugin boundary

controls: The current installed desktop application and its supported OS, accessibility and deployment behavior.
Keep the UI and native-service contract fixed; shell, renderer, language and virtualization are separate variables.
test_plans.decision: which complete desktop configuration meets the application's actual platform and interaction requirements?
gates: feature parity, safe privileged IPC, complete records, accessibility, required webview behavior, and deployment correctness.
metrics: installed cold startup, input-to-usable and fully verified results, p95 input delay, peak process-tree memory, package size, and maintenance effort. A smaller shell is insufficient if a required workflow fails.
protocol: Use the same UI and native-service contract for import, full-record search, large-card filtering, keyboard navigation, details, cancellation, durable save/reopen, update, and uninstall. Test supported Windows/macOS/Linux targets separately; include the current application's deployment and accessibility behavior.

For a Windows-native cohort, add WinUI/Windows App SDK; compare Avalonia, Slint or egui only when the same required feature set can be implemented. Keep renderer, shell and language changes as separate declared variables. Virtualize presentation while retaining the complete collection and stable item identities. Include variable-height rows, media load/error, rapid filter/sort, keyboard focus, selection, screen readers, IME, high DPI and insert/delete while scrolling. TanStack Virtual and native collection virtualization are role-specific tools, not whole-app substitutes.
test_plans.title: Desktop vertical slice

controls: The pinned production and development toolchain for one unchanged application.
Keep required type checking, emitted behavior and cache conditions equivalent.
test_plans.decision: which compatible toolchain reduces the real edit-to-validated-preview loop?
gates: route behavior, asset paths, source maps, type diagnostics, plugin compatibility, and executable output parity.
metrics: clean builds, incremental rebuilds, HMR-to-usable UI, type-check time, peak RSS, output bytes, and setup effort. Cache state and type-check omission cannot explain a claimed win.
protocol: Compare pinned production and development builds for one unchanged application. Vite is an application build driver, while Rolldown and Rspack are bundling components: compare complete supported configurations, not unrelated layer names. Include a declared type-checking baseline and, when compatible, TypeScript's native compiler as a separate variable.
test_plans.title: Frontend build and edit loop

controls: The current service runtime with the same supported handler, dependencies and validation.
Pin framework and runtime independently; a no-op HTTP handler is a separate microbenchmark.
test_plans.decision: does Node.js, Bun, or Deno improve a small real service under its required contract?
gates: response/body parity, TLS/auth behavior where required, cancellation, backpressure, dependency compatibility, and preserved errors.
metrics: p50/p95/p99 request latency, throughput at a fixed error/latency budget, startup, RSS, and deployment burden. A no-op HTTP benchmark is a separate microbenchmark.
protocol: Run an identical supported handler and dependency set with validation, database calls, structured logging, cancellation, and errors included. Use concurrency and payload distributions representative of the target. Pin framework and runtime versions independently and record unsupported dependencies.
test_plans.title: JavaScript service runtime

controls: The current engine and complete interactive scene using fixed assets, quality and scripted behavior.
Separate native/browser and 2D/3D cohorts; add equivalent physics only where required.
test_plans.decision: which engine fits the target's rendering, asset, editing, and export needs?
gates: visual and behavioral acceptance, import fidelity, input responsiveness, required export formats, target-device operation, and license compatibility.
metrics: frame-time distribution, load/import time, memory/VRAM, iteration time, binary size, and implementation effort. Missing features are disqualifications, not faster frame times.
protocol: Implement the same small interactive scene and asset-import workflow in the pinned baseline, Bevy, and Godot where the required target platforms are supported. Fix assets, lighting/quality settings, scripted behaviors, input, animation, and scene complexity. Preserve the target mod/tool ecosystem's pinned compatibility requirements.

For browser-specific slices, compare complete Three.js or PixiJS configurations in separate 3D/2D cohorts; add Rapier only where equivalent physics is required. Separate renderer/API migration from engine replacement. Record unsupported shaders, post-processing, physics determinism assumptions, browser fallback, context loss and export restrictions as eligibility outcomes. Browser export and native rendering cannot share a frame-time ranking without equivalent hardware and visual work.
test_plans.title: Game/tool vertical slice

controls: The current search implementation and a SQLite FTS5 or Tantivy lexical reference for exact identifiers, names and paths.
Use held-out relevance labels with identical corpus, filters and resource limits; keep dense, lexical and hybrid configurations distinct.
test_plans.decision: which retrieval system best serves the catalog's actual search queries at the required quality?
gates: minimum declared recall/relevance, filter correctness, update visibility, and failure/recovery requirements.
metrics: recall@k, nDCG@10, p95/p99 latency, build/update time, index size, and full-service resource cost. Report the quality/latency tradeoff; do not rank a lower-recall run as an unconditional winner.
protocol: Compare pgvector, Qdrant, LanceDB, and Milvus using the same corpus, embedding model, ground-truth neighbors, query labels, filter selectivities, updates, and resource limits. Maintain distinct dense, lexical, and hybrid configurations. Preserve code identifiers, exact terms, and tenant boundaries in the test set.

Keep a SQLite FTS5 or Tantivy lexical baseline for exact identifiers, names and paths. Add semantic or hybrid retrieval only when held-out relevance labels show the extra system is useful. Browser IndexedDB/Dexie persistence is a separate host contract; do not compare its transaction latency to a remote vector service as one storage score.
test_plans.title: Labeled catalog retrieval

controls: The current supported local runtime on the same hardware/OS and model configuration.
Fix weights, quantization, tokenizer, context and generation settings; separate loading, prompt processing and generation.
test_plans.decision: which supported local runtime meets a desktop assistant's response and memory requirements?
gates: required task quality, complete output, supported context, deterministic settings where available, memory fit, and target packaging.
metrics: time to first token, inter-token latency, prompt/decode throughput, peak RAM/VRAM, energy where instrumented, and setup burden. Cross-hardware results need separate cohorts; quantization changes need separate configurations.
protocol: Compare llama.cpp, MLX LM, and MLC LLM only within hardware/OS combinations each supports. Fix model identity, weights, quantization, tokenizer, context, generation settings, task set, and output-quality gates. Separate initial model loading, prompt processing, and generation.
test_plans.title: Local model inference

controls: The uninstrumented owned reference scene/import pipeline with seeded known faults.
Use a common tracing event scope; evaluate RenderDoc frame debugging separately.
test_plans.decision: which instrumentation exposes the target's frame, scheduling, allocation, or graphics fault with acceptable overhead?
gates: required event/fault visibility, usable saved traces, supported graphics APIs/OS, and bounded capture overhead.
metrics: diagnosis accuracy/time, frame-time overhead, event loss, trace size, and analysis memory. Do not combine distinct profiler roles into one score.
protocol: Seed known performance and correctness faults in an owned reference scene/import pipeline. Compare uninstrumented execution with Tracy and Perfetto using a common event scope. Evaluate RenderDoc's frame-debugging task in a separate graphics-debugging cohort; it performs a different job from continuous CPU tracing.
test_plans.title: Desktop profiling effectiveness

controls: The current serving configuration on matching supported GPUs, weights, precision and request traces.
Separate cold and warm cache lanes and vary attention, speculative decoding or KV caching independently.
test_plans.decision: which serving configuration gives the best useful capacity within a latency and quality budget?
gates: model/output-quality equivalence, request completion, declared latency SLO, memory limits, and timeout accounting.
metrics: goodput meeting the SLO, time to first token, inter-token tails, GPU memory, energy where measured, and cost per completed valid task. Provisioning and resource spending are separate execution decisions.
protocol: Compare vLLM, SGLang, and TensorRT-LLM on matching supported GPU configurations, model weights, precision, context lengths, request traces, and batching policies. Run cold and warm cache lanes separately. Introduce attention kernels, speculative decoding, or KV-cache systems one variable at a time.
test_plans.title: GPU inference serving

controls: The current complete model/agent/harness configuration under one fixed benchmark protocol and held-out split.
Fix reasoning effort, permissions, network, token/time/cost and retry policy; keep different benchmark protocols in separate cohorts.
test_plans.decision: which complete agent configuration resolves target-like work reliably within a fixed budget?
